content:
We need to return the mapped_rxn associated with the template that, when applied to the molecule, reproduces the reaction described (intramolecular Michael addition cyclization of chalcone to flavanone). The molecule is the product flavanone: O=C1C(C2=CC=CC=C2)C3=CC=CC=C3O1 (a flavanone). We need a retrosynthetic template that breaks it into chalcone precursor (open chain). The search gave many templates but not necessarily correct. The first result (reaction_id 162961) seems relevant: It shows a mapped_rxn where product is flavanone (product_smiles) and reactants are chalcone-like? Let's examine mapped_rxn from that entry:

mapped_rxn: '[CH3:16][C:15]1=[CH:14][CH:13]=[C:12]([OH:11])[CH:18]=[CH:17]1.[CH3:1][CH2:2][O:3][C:4]1=[CH:5][CH:6]=[C:7]([CH:8](O)[C:9](=[O:10])O)[CH:19]=[CH:20]1>>[CH3:1][CH2:2][O:3][C:4]1=[CH:5][CH:6]=[C:7]([CH:8]2[C:9](=[O:10])[O:11][C:12]3=[C:13]2[CH:14]=[C:15]([CH3:16])[CH:17]=[CH:18]3)[CH:19]=[CH:20]1'

Product side is after >>? Actually mapped_rxn format: reactants >> products. Here left side: two fragments: a phenyl with OH? first fragment: [CH3:16][C:15]1=[CH:14][CH:13]=[C:12]([OH:11])[CH:18]=[CH:17]1 (that's a phenyl with OH and methyl). second fragment: [CH3:1][CH2:2][O:3][C:4]1=[CH:5][CH:6]=[C:7]([CH:8](O)[C:9](=[O:10])O)[CH:19]=[CH:20]1 (that's a phenyl with side chain carbonyl etc). The product is flavanone core. This seems exactly the cyclization of chalcone (two phenyl rings). So this template likely matches our target. The template_id is integer? The entry includes template_hash and reaction_id. The template_id to return is the one used to search the database not the hash. The template_id likely equals reaction_id? In earlier tasks, template_id is integer (e.g., 264979). So we can use reaction_id as template_id. For this entry, reaction_id = 162961. So we need to return mapped_rxn and template_id = 162961.

Check if applying this template to our molecule works. Could test apply_template with template_id 162961.
